title: How to avoid disaster when vibe-coding a billing engine — Andrew Garvin, Stripe
talk_summary: Stripe/Metronome demo shows an agent provisioning a sandbox billing setup from natural language, guided by portable skills files and agent-readable errors. The speaker argues for sandboxed, human-in-the-loop use of coding agents for business-critical billing and for spend controls such as agent wallets.

takeaways.what_they_do: They maintain extensible skill files that give the coding agent context about Metronome's API and implementation footguns.
takeaways.evidence_quote: building an extensible set of skills files that can provide context to the agent that's implementing metronome and working with our API

takeaways.what_they_do: They design errors to be verbose and clear enough that the agent can diagnose and self-correct without human intervention.
takeaways.evidence_quote: have much more verbose and clear errors so that the agent can self-correct

takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly avoid letting the agent operate the whole business-critical system without a human in the loop, and they build a sandbox experience for testing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: not to have a customer operate the entire system without a human in the loop

takeaways.what_they_do: They propose giving agents a wallet they can spend from, with controls at that level to limit runaway spend.
takeaways.evidence_quote: having agents have a wallet um that they only they can spend from and having controls at that level

takeaways.what_they_do: Their skill files direct the agent to flow usage into the sandbox platform so the setup can be tested against realistic customer-like usage.
takeaways.evidence_quote: directing um the agent to actually flow usage into the metronome platform
